body:
Third "Aggressive ships" run defects: #736 (AGG-10), #737 (AGG-T03), #740 (advisory). Refs #736, Refs #737, Refs #740.

## #736: keychain under Aggressive (assessment + truthful wording)
**The boundary holds.** On macOS the Aggressive sandbox never reaches the keychain service: `com.apple.SecurityServer` is only allowed by `seatbelt_network_policy.sbpl`, which Aggressive (network off) never adds, and `~/Library/Keychains` is a denied read.
Evidence (real `sandbox-exec`, a disposable keychain file made with `HOME`/`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` pointed at a temp folder; the login keychain and search list were never touched, checked before/after):
- outside any sandbox: `security find-generic-password -s probe736 -w <tmp keychain>` → the canary;
- workspace-write sandbox with network **on** (Permissive-like): → the canary;
- workspace-write sandbox with network **off** (Aggressive's): the keychain file itself is readable (21744 bytes), but `security` answers `SecKeychainSearchCopyNext: The specified item could not be found` (exit 44). Same answer as AGG-10.

So AGG-10's command ran but could not read anything. What was wrong is the wording: the prompt talked about credential files and the vault, and the result had no attribution. Now, under Aggressive on macOS:
- the prompt for a `security` keychain verb says the keychain is out of reach of agent commands, the command runs but can't read/add/change items, never granted; no Grant once (it was offered before when no untrusted content had arrived);
- where it fails, the result says the "could not be found" comes from Aggressive, not from the keychain's contents; the inspector lists "using the macOS keychain".

Regression test (real Seatbelt): `core/tests/suite/issue_736_740.rs::issue_736_keychain_is_out_of_reach_and_explained` creates a disposable keychain, proves the item is readable outside the sandbox, then approves the command in an Aggressive session: the secret never appears, and the prompt/warning/inspector say why.

The keychain text is used only on macOS with network off and no network proxy (`turn.network` is `None`). Residual, not changed (it would move the boundary): if a managed network proxy is enforced (an enterprise requirements file), Seatbelt appends the network policy, which allows `com.apple.SecurityServer`, also under Aggressive; Corbanu then makes no keychain claim. Contained Claude panes run with `enforce_managed_network` too.

## #737: config writers outside the folder
`git config` (`--global` → `~/.gitconfig`, `--system`, `--file`, the repository's `.git/config`), `npm config set|delete|edit` / `npm set` (`~/.npmrc`, `--userconfig`, `--location=project`), `pip config set|unset|edit` (user / `--global`) and `gh config set` are recognised as writes of that file. Reads (`--get`, `--list`, `get`, a key alone) are not. `git config --global` therefore gets the #620 start-up-file treatment (no Grant once, the explanation in the prompt and where it fails); `~/.npmrc` and pip's config get the new outside-the-folder explanation.

## #740: no Grant once where it can't apply
The prompt leaves Grant once out, and says why, when the command's text shows every write and none is something Grant once lifts, and the command
- writes outside the current folder (`echo t04 >> ../outside-notes.txt`, `/tmp`),
- writes a read-only part of the folder that no grant lifts (the project's `.git`: `printf … > .git/hooks/pre-commit`, `git config core.hooksPath /tmp`),
- (#584, extended to `mkdir`/`rmdir`) writes `.codex`/`.agents` (`mkdir .agents`, AGG-R13),
- or its text shows every write and none is liftable (`cat .codex/notes.md`, `ln -s notes.txt notes-link.txt && cat notes-link.txt`).
"Liftable" is decided as `ReadDenials::apply` decides it: a read-only path the session's own profile could otherwise write. A command whose writes the text can't show (scripts, `npm install`, `cd`, substitutions, newlines, `sed`, `cp -t`, a variable set for a config writer, unresolvable `$VAR` paths) keeps the offer, as before, even with an outside write beside it (#620/#584 still withhold it for start-up files outside the folder and `.codex`/`.agents`). Like #584/#620 this only withholds an offer and adds an explanation; it never changes what runs or what is denied. Not on Windows (it enforces writes differently, #554). Permissive and Moderate are unchanged (Aggressive only).

## Tests
- Unit: `protected_reads_writes_tests.rs` (config writers, understood commands, keychain detection, the notes under Aggressive's profile incl. a `.husky` hook that keeps the grant and a home-folder session).
- Real sandbox: `issue_736_740.rs` — fails before the fix (all 3: Grant once offered for the keychain command, `~/.gitconfig`, `../outside`), passes after.
- Existing suites `issue_584`, `issue_620_622`, `pf_25_s01`, `pf_23_s01`, `issue_623`, `issue_506` pass.

## Gate
- Fail-before/pass-after (real sandbox): `issue_736_740.rs` — macOS 3/3 fail before (Grant once offered for the keychain command, `~/.gitconfig`, `../outside`), 3/3 pass after; glitch (bubblewrap, `ulimit -n 65536`): 2/2 (#737, #740) fail before, pass after.
- Focused `just test -p codex-core --test-threads 4 -E 'test(/security::|suite::issue_|suite::pf_2|suite::pf_30|suite::provenance|suite::approvals/)'` (TMPDIR=/tmp): 474/474 plain, 474/474 with `developer-accounting`. (A full-parallel run on the loaded Mac timed out in security suites unrelated to this change, e.g. `issue_651`, `issue_506`; with 4 threads all pass.)
- glitch: `cargo test -p codex-core --lib -- protected_reads security::` 362/362; `--test all` security suites (issue_736_740, issue_620_622, issue_584, pf_25_s01, pf_23_s01, issue_623, issue_506) 29/29 + pf_23_s01 19/19.
- Clippy `-D warnings --tests`: macOS and Linux (glitch), plain and `developer-accounting`, clean.
- Review: Opus 5.5 High — REQUEST_CHANGES on ff0e70c8a5 (7 findings, all fixed), APPROVE on a79ff79b39; short re-review of the evidence-only commit on the final head.
- tmux replays (GLM 5.3 Flash on zai, debug build of a79ff79b39, disposable home and HOME): `qa/security-levels/fixes/issue-736-740-20261014/` (prompts without Grant once, results with the explanations).
- Videos: [#736](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/releases/download/demos/issue-736-issue736-keychain-explained-a79ff79b392a-2026-10-13.mp4), [#737](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/releases/download/demos/issue-737-issue737-gitconfig-no-grant-a79ff79b392a-2026-10-13.mp4), [#740](https://github.com/CorbanuCore/CorbanuTerminal/releases/download/demos/issue-740-issue740-no-grant-where-useless-a79ff79b392a-2026-10-13.mp4).
title: Aggressive: explain keychain commands (#736); no Grant once where it cannot apply (#737, #740)
